CONTEXT.goal: Verify whether OTA query can keep operational coverage without DOM fallback and reclassify it from hold if the PoC is decisive.
CONTEXT.summary: The app-centric transition plan left OTA query on hold because `fetchProviderRows` mixes API-first loading with DOM fallback/merge when coverage is too low.
constraints: Work on one problem only: OTA query coverage without DOM fallback.
Do not declare app-first without verification evidence.
Keep the code change minimal and non-destructive.

symptoms: The transition plan classified OTA query as hold because DOM fallback coverage safety was unverified.
`fetchProviderRows` falls back to DOM rows when provider API fails or coverage is below threshold.

ROOT_CAUSE.summary: OTA query is not purely app-first today because low-coverage API responses still rely on the DOM merge branch to recover acceptable coverage.
evidence: Code inspection showed `fetchProviderRows` uses `assessProviderRowsCoverage` and merges DOM rows whenever API coverage is unacceptable.
The new PoC reproduced both providers with 9/9 API-only coverage in the healthy path and 3 API + 6 DOM rows in the degraded path.

ACTION.summary: Exported the shared coverage helper, added a regression-style PoC for Station and Naver, and reclassified OTA query from hold to bridge-candidate in the architecture document.
changes: Exposed `assessProviderRowsCoverage` from `src/io/pms.fetch.js` for testable PoC measurement.
Added `tests/regression_ota_dom_fallback_poc.mjs` to compare API-only and degraded API+DOM scenarios.
Updated `docs/architecture/APP_CENTRIC_TRANSITION_PLAN.md` to record the PoC result and move OTA query to `bridge-candidate`.

procedures.name: Legacy branch and constraint review
evidence: No unrelated files were changed and the DOM fallback logic itself was not expanded.

OUTCOME.summary: The small PoC was decisive enough to move OTA query from hold to bridge-candidate, not app-first.
verified_facts: Both providers satisfied the current coverage threshold with API-only full-grid responses.
Both providers still needed DOM merge to recover acceptable coverage from degraded 3-row API responses.
The transition document now reflects OTA query as `bridge-candidate`.
remaining_risks: The PoC does not measure how often low-coverage API responses occur in live sessions.

use_when: A migration plan is blocked on whether an API-first feature is truly app-first or still needs a bridge for degraded coverage.
A shared fetcher has an explicit fallback branch and you need a minimal, reproducible classification PoC.
avoid_when: The feature still lacks a clear API-first path or the fallback branch cannot be isolated in code.
REUSE_RULE.fallback: If production frequency is still disputed after the harness PoC, add runtime instrumentation before promoting the feature to app-first.
